findings.section: The record type decides what kind of value a name returns; FAQ quick-fire FAQ 4; 1-fast.md Choose it or not / Alias record or CNAME record
findings.quote: Each record has a **routing policy** and a time to live (TTL): how long resolvers can cache it. Records [must have a TTL](../facts/route53.md#route53-ttl-required-on-all-records).
findings.evidence: Three TTL statements meet her and are never reconciled: 2-deep 'Records must have a TTL', FAQ 4 'There is no default TTL.' and the 1-fast compare row 'Who sets the TTL? For an AWS resource, Route 53 uses the default TTL for the resource | You do'. From the skim, 'no default TTL' and 'the default TTL for the resource' look like a contradiction. Fact route53-alias-to-aws-resource-ttl-not-settable: 'If an alias record points to an AWS resource, you can't set the time to live (TTL); Route 53 uses the default TTL for the resource.' Add one clause to step 4 ('you set it on every record except an alias record to an AWS resource, which takes the TTL of the resource') and the same exception to FAQ 4's answer. (Repeated from the first review, reader-04; not changed in edit.)
findings.resolution: fix-13: step 4 now says 'A non-alias record [must have a TTL]. For an alias record to an AWS resource, [Route 53 uses the default TTL for the resource].' FAQ 4 now answers 'There is no default TTL: you set it on each non-alias record.' The 1-fast row 'Who sets the TTL?' already gives the same split, so the three statements now agree.

findings.section: Failover records answer with the secondary only while the primary is unhealthy
findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** The primary failover record is an alias record for three weighted records, with Evaluate Target Health set to Yes. Two servers fail. Does Route 53 switch?
findings.evidence: The answer depends on a fact the stem leaves out: whether the three weighted records have health checks. The chapter itself teaches that a record without a health check is 'always' considered healthy (fact route53-record-without-health-check-always-healthy), so without health checks Route 53 sees no failed server at all, and the answer 'at least one of the associated resources healthy' (route53-failover-multiple-primary-healthy-if-one-healthy) teaches the wrong reason. Add 'each with a health check' to the stem.
findings.resolution: fix-13: the Stop and answer now says 'three weighted records, each with a health check, and Evaluate Target Health is set to Yes'.

findings.section: An alias record can answer at the zone apex where a CNAME record cannot

Why the DNS protocol forbids a CNAME record at the apex is stated as a rule only (route53-cname-dns-protocol-forbids-zone-apex). The tasks.json t02 read-only alternative already gives the cause in plain words ('The apex holds the NS and SOA records'). If a verified fact states that a CNAME record cannot share its name with other records, add that cause; otherwise keep the rule and add 'and alias queries to AWS resources are free' to tie the Why to the section.
findings.resolution: fix-13: no verified fact states the cause (a CNAME record cannot share its name with other records), so the cause cannot enter the book; the rule stays with its fact. 2-deep.md is at 4496 of its 4500 words, so the extra clause does not fit either.

findings.section: route53-t02 and route53-t03 steps 2 and 3
findings.quote: Two later commands need the short zone ID, the part after /hostedzone/: write it where they show <ZONE_ID>.
findings.evidence: The tasks mix $ZONE_ID (the path /hostedzone/ID, captured) and <ZONE_ID> (the short ID, typed by hand) in neighbouring commands. READER.md: she acts before she reads; a pasted command with the literal '<ZONE_ID>' fails. Either use one form everywhere (if the commands accept the full path, use $ZONE_ID in all of them), or make the hand-typed value a named variable set once in step 2 (SHORT_ID=...) and use $SHORT_ID in every later command, so no command keeps a placeholder.
